title: Leonardo's Monorail
description: Implement an assembunny interpreter with four registers and four instructions, then run the boot sequence to find the password.
writeup:
## Approach

This puzzle introduces *assembunny*, a simple assembly-like language that recurs in later 2016 puzzles. The interpreter needs four operations on four integer registers (`a`, `b`, `c`, `d`):

- `cpy x y` — copy value or register into a register
- `inc x` / `dec x` — increment or decrement a register
- `jnz x y` — conditional relative jump (skip if zero)

The key detail is that `cpy` and `jnz` accept either a register name or a literal integer as their first argument, so a small helper (`val`) resolves either case.

## Part 1

Start all registers at 0, run the program until the instruction pointer falls outside the program, and return register `a`.

## Part 2

The only difference is that register `c` starts at `1` instead of `0`. This changes the control flow — a `jnz c ...` branch near the start takes a different path — resulting in a much larger value in `a`. The interpreter itself is completely unchanged.
